zone_note: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map (2023 edition). Each zone covers a 10 F band of average annual extreme minimum winter temperature; a and b sub-zones split each band in half. Zones describe winter cold only. Frost dates vary within a zone, so each garden pack stores its own frost data.

packs.name: Tracy City, TN (Zone 7a)
packs.zone_note: Tracy City sits on the Cumberland Plateau at higher elevation, and the surrounding valleys are Zone 7b. Confirm the zone for your exact ZIP at planthardiness.ars.usda.gov.

frost.base_source: NOAA 1991-2020 normals, Soddy-Daisy-Mowbray Mtn station (1,699 ft), 30% probability
frost.elevation_note: Higher ground usually means a later last spring frost and an earlier first fall frost. The shift is editable. Set it to 0 to use the station dates as they are.

extension.name: University of Tennessee Extension
extension.note: Check the UT Extension county office for current planting calendars and local wild-food guidance.

planting.note: Cool-season. Sow before the last frost.
Plant sets once the soil can be worked.
Plant seed potatoes about two weeks before the last frost.
Transplant before warm weather sets in.
Warm-season. Plant after the soil warms.
Tender. Protect from any late cold snap.

packs.planting_note: These windows are general starting points, counted from the frost dates above, not a substitute for an extension calendar. Harvest days are typical averages.

wild_edibles.name: Wild garlic (ramps)
wild_edibles.lookalike: Lily of the valley is poisonous and can look like wild garlic.
wild_edibles.warning: Confirm by smell as well as leaf shape. Wild garlic smells like onion or garlic, and lily of the valley doesn't.

wild_edibles.name: Purslane
wild_edibles.lookalike: Prostrate spurge is poisonous and often grows next to purslane.
wild_edibles.warning: Check the leaves and stems carefully before eating.

wild_edibles.name: Wild carrot (Queen Anne's lace)
wild_edibles.lookalike: Poison hemlock is a deadly carrot-family plant, not the hemlock tree. It can look very similar to wild carrot.
wild_edibles.warning: Many plants in this carrot family look alike, and some are deadly. Don't eat any of them unless you have identified it with certainty using a field guide.

wild_edibles.name: Blueberries and huckleberries
wild_edibles.lookalike: Deadly nightshade berries can look like blueberries.
wild_edibles.warning: Eat only berries you have identified on the bush. Don't eat berries of unknown origin.

wild_edibles.name: Cattail
wild_edibles.lookalike: Iris plants grow in similar areas and are toxic.
wild_edibles.warning: Identify by the brown seed heads and by the way it grows in standing water.

wild_edible_rules: Before eating any wild plant, be 100 percent certain it is correctly identified. Use at least three different plant guides.
When in doubt, leave it out.
Don't forage from roadsides, sprayed fields or other areas that may have been treated with herbicides or pesticides.
Check local rules before collecting on public land or from protected plants.
